reason: Correct on the 65SC12. INC A (&1A) is a real 65C02/65SC12 opcode in a cmos = TRUE section. Old: count+1+1 (SEC; ADC #1) then CLC; ADC p_ptr = p_ptr+count+2, C the carry of the last add (valid for count<=253). New: INC A; SEC; ADC p_ptr = p_ptr+count+2 with the same C for count<=253 (and for count=254 the new one is even right where the old wrapped). Only C is consumed (BCC same_page); N/Z/V overwritten by INC sky_c/LDA/CMP. No SED anywhere in the build, so no decimal-mode difference. Cycles: old SEC 2 + ADC # 2 + CLC 2 + ADC zp 3 = 9; new INC A 2 + SEC 2 + ADC zp 3 = 7: 2 saved per execution as claimed. Bytes miscounted in the claim: p_ptr is zero page &AA, so old is 1+2+1+2 = 6 bytes and new 1+1+2 = 4: 2 bytes saved, not 1. Everything after moves down 2 within &C2AA-&C2DD (all in page &C2): BCC same_page, BEQ built, JMP column, JSR row_ptr are symbolic; row_ptr's LDA sky_rb,Y and sky_blk_lo/hi,Y reads are absolute table reads whose bases do not move. No self-modified operands after the change (src/pix are before it); the copy loop uses hazel_c_end - &C200, so it copies 2 fewer bytes correctly; sky_build at &C200 does not move.
